name: Azure Data Factory
sku: Azure Data Factory (ADF). Microsoft documents Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric as its next generation, so new projects on Fabric should look at fabric-data-factory instead.

ingest.batch-extract.note: The Copy activity moves data from on-premises and cloud sources (SaaS services, databases, file shares, FTP and web services) into a central store, with broad connectivity, compression, and data preview and validation.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: Pipelines group activities that can be chained in sequence or run in parallel, with control flow for branching, parameters and For-each loops.

orchestrate.scheduling.note: Pipelines run from triggers that decide when an execution starts, including a daily schedule.

orchestrate.event-triggers.note: Custom event triggers run an action when a certain event occurs, and a pipeline can be started when files land in a blob container.

orchestrate.ci-cd.note: Full support for CI/CD of data pipelines using Azure DevOps and GitHub, so ETL processes can be developed incrementally before publishing.

bands.note: Built-in monitoring of scheduled activities and pipelines for success and failure rates, through Azure Monitor, API, PowerShell, Azure Monitor logs and health panels in the Azure portal.
Microsoft Entra ID integration and role-based access control decide who can use data flows and pipelines.

proposed_capabilities.name: Visual self-service data preparation
proposed_capabilities.description: Point-and-click combining, cleaning and shaping of data aimed at analysts, without writing SQL or Spark code. Mapping data flows build transformation graphs that run on a managed Spark cluster the user never operates.

presentation.tagline: Managed pipelines to copy, transform and schedule data across Azure and beyond.
